question: How is precision calculated?
options: True positives divided by all predicted positives
True negatives divided by all actual negatives
Correct predictions divided by total predictions
True positives divided by all actual positives
explanation: Precision answers: of everything predicted positive, how much was actually positive.

subject: ai
question: Which metric is commonly used to evaluate a regression model?
options: F1 score
Precision
Recall
Mean squared error
explanation: Mean squared error averages squared differences between predicted and actual values; the others are classification metrics.

subject: ai
question: What does accuracy measure for a classifier?
options: The fraction of all predictions that are correct
The fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive
The fraction of actual positives that are detected
The average squared difference between predictions and targets
explanation: Accuracy is the number of correct predictions divided by the total number of predictions.

subject: ai
question: In binary classification, what is a false positive?
options: Predicting the negative class when the actual class is positive
Correctly predicting the negative class
Correctly predicting the positive class
Predicting the positive class when the actual class is negative
explanation: A false positive is a false alarm, such as flagging a legitimate email as spam.

subject: ai
question: How is recall calculated?
options: True positives divided by all predicted positives
False positives divided by all actual negatives
True positives divided by all actual positives
True negatives divided by all predicted negatives
explanation: Recall answers: of all real positives, how many did the model find.

subject: ai
question: What does a confusion matrix show?
options: The correlation between every pair of input features
The gradients of each layer during backpropagation
The loss value at each training epoch
Counts of predicted classes versus actual classes
explanation: A confusion matrix tabulates true and false positives and negatives, from which many metrics are derived.

subject: ai
question: For cancer screening, where missing a real case is very costly, which metric should be prioritized?
options: Precision
Specificity
Recall
Accuracy
explanation: Recall measures the share of actual positives detected, so maximizing it minimizes missed cases.

subject: ai
question: What does a ROC AUC of 0.5 indicate?
options: The model detects exactly half of the positives
The model ranks positives no better than random guessing
The model always predicts the positive class
The model is perfectly calibrated
explanation: AUC is the probability a random positive is scored above a random negative; 0.5 means chance-level ranking.

subject: ai
question: What is the F1 score?
options: The harmonic mean of precision and recall
The arithmetic mean of precision and recall
The product of accuracy and recall
The area under the ROC curve
explanation: F1 uses the harmonic mean, so it is high only when both precision and recall are high.

subject: ai
question: What does a ROC curve plot?
options: Precision against recall at a single threshold
Training loss against the number of epochs
True positive rate against false positive rate across decision thresholds
Accuracy against dataset size
explanation: Sweeping the threshold traces the trade-off between catching positives and raising false alarms.

subject: ai
question: What does R-squared measure for a regression model?
options: The average absolute prediction error
The proportion of the target's variance explained by the model
The number of features in the model
The correlation between two input features
explanation: An R-squared of 1 means a perfect fit, while 0 means the model does no better than predicting the mean.

subject: ai
question: In a dataset where 1% of transactions are fraud, why is accuracy a poor metric?
options: Accuracy cannot be computed for binary problems
Accuracy always penalizes false negatives too heavily
Accuracy requires probability outputs rather than labels
A model predicting not fraud for everything scores 99% accuracy
explanation: With heavy class imbalance, a trivial majority-class predictor looks excellent on accuracy while catching no fraud.

subject: ai
question: For a heavily imbalanced dataset where the positive class matters most, which curve is usually more informative?
options: The ROC curve, since a large negative class makes it more sensitive
The precision-recall curve, since ROC can look optimistic when negatives dominate
The calibration curve, since it measures ranking quality
The learning curve, since it plots loss against epochs
explanation: False positive rate barely moves when negatives are abundant, while precision directly exposes the cost of false positives.

subject: ai
question: Which kind of prediction does log loss (cross-entropy) penalize most heavily?
options: A confident prediction that turns out to be wrong
An uncertain prediction that turns out to be right
A correct prediction made with 100% confidence
Any prediction for the majority class
explanation: The penalty -log(p) grows without bound as the probability assigned to the true class approaches zero.

subject: ai
question: What does it mean for a classifier to be well calibrated?
options: It achieves the highest possible ROC AUC
Its predicted probabilities match observed frequencies, e.g. 70% predictions are right about 70% of the time
It has equal precision and recall
It predicts each class equally often
explanation: Calibration concerns whether probabilities can be trusted as probabilities, which is separate from ranking quality.

subject: ai
question: In multiclass classification, how does macro-averaged F1 differ from micro-averaged F1?
options: Macro uses only the largest class, while micro uses only the smallest
They are always equal for any dataset
Macro is computed on training data, while micro is computed on test data
Macro averages per-class F1 scores equally, while micro pools all counts so frequent classes dominate
explanation: Macro-F1 highlights performance on rare classes, while micro-F1 reflects overall per-example performance.

subject: ai
question: Raising a classifier's decision threshold typically has what effect?
options: Recall rises and precision falls
Precision rises and recall falls
Both precision and recall rise
ROC AUC changes significantly
explanation: A higher threshold makes fewer, more confident positive predictions, trading missed positives for fewer false alarms.

subject: ai
question: How does RMSE differ from MAE as a regression metric?
options: RMSE penalizes large errors more heavily because errors are squared
RMSE and MAE always rank models identically
MAE penalizes large errors more heavily because it uses absolute values
RMSE is unaffected by outliers
explanation: Squaring magnifies big errors, so RMSE is more sensitive to outliers than MAE.
